chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not neglect the ghusl on the day of Friday, for it is a Sunnah, and smell the perfume, and wear the best of your clothes, and let your completion of the ghusl be before the midday sun passes (Zawal). So when it passes, stand up, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The ghusl is obligatory on the day of Friday.'

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: Midday (when the sun passes its zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and etiquette for Friday ghusl in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (asws) establishes the Friday ritual bath (ghusl) as obligatory (wajib), linking physical purification with spiritual adornment through scent and attire. It emphasizes the importance of performing the bath before midday (zawal) to ensure readiness for the congregational prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both external decorum and internal tranquility (sakinah) during worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not neglect the washing (shower) on the day of Friday, for it is a Sunnah, and wear the perfume, and wear the best of your clothes, and let you take the shower before the midday. So when it is midday, stand, and upon you should be the tranquillity and the dignity’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The shower is Obligatory on the day of Friday’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must not ignore Ghusl (bath) on Friday; it is a sunnah.

You should use perfumes, dress up in you proper dress and you should complete your Ghusl (bath) before noontime. At Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) rise up with calmness and dignity for prayer.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Ghusl (bath) on Friday is obligatory.’”
